title: Adaptive Admin Toolbox for Semi-Automated Support Sessions
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build an adaptive admin toolbox that turns runbooks into composable, idempotent micro-actions and supports semi-automated interactive support sessions. The goal is to reduce MTTD/MTTR for common support scenarios while preserving safety, auditability, and the ability to revert actions quickly. This ticket covers the end-to-end prototype: CLI + Console integration, session recording, a safe execution sandbox for dry runs, autosuggested next steps driven by historical incident traces, and RBAC/audit hooks for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Engineers can execute a curated task bundle (3+ idempotent micro-actions) from the Console with a dry-run checkbox and receive a structured result summary.
2) Every executed action is recorded with context, user, token, and can be replayed in the sandbox within 72 hours.
3) Autosuggest engine surface shows at least 3 candidate next-steps based on prior incidents for the same alert category with confidence scores.
4) RBAC policies prevent non-admins from running destructive actions; destructive actions require 2-step confirmation or an allowlist.
5) Telemetry emits per-action latency, success/failure, and rollback events to the ops dashboard and traces link back to the Console route.
6) Security review completed and integration with KMS for audit log signing is validated in staging.
7) Rollout plan includes a canary group (internal SREs) and a rollback path documented in a runbook.
8) Unit and integration tests cover idempotency guarantees and dry-run parity for all micro-actions in the prototype bundle.
implementation_steps: Design task schema for micro-actions: inputs, outputs, side-effects, idempotency markers, timeout semantics.
Implement a lightweight sandbox runner that can execute micro-actions in dry-run mode and capture simulated side-effects.
Add Console surface: task composer, dry-run toggle, action preview, and session recorder (metadata + diffs).
Build autosuggest pipeline: cluster historical incident traces, map alert signatures to candidate task sequences, expose confidence score metadata.
Integrate RBAC hooks + 2-step confirmations; enforce allowlists for high-risk actions via policy service.
Wire telemetry: per-action metrics, execution traces, rollback markers; publish to ops dashboards and SLOs.
Create end-to-end e2e tests, staging rollout plan, and a canary release for the SRE cohort.
Complete security review and KMS-signed audit logs before broad rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Autosuggest proposes unsafe actions. Mitigation: Show confidence and provenance, default to read-only suggestions, require confirmation for any state change.

Risk: Dry-run diverges from real-run due to external side-effects. Mitigation: Capture service call signatures during dry-run and compare against canary executions; require signoff for actions with non-deterministic side-effects.
Risk: Permission misuse. Mitigation: Tight RBAC defaults, ephemeral elevation tokens for short windows, audit log alarms for abnormal patterns.
Risk: Increased alert fatigue from suggested flows. Mitigation: Tune suggestion suppression thresholds and provide opt-out in Console preferences.
testing_plan: Unit tests for task schema validation and idempotency invariants.
Integration tests for sandbox runner vs real runner parity on small stateful services (KV store mock, model-kv cache clear).
Chaos test: simulate partial failures mid-sequence and assert correct rollback/compensation behavior.
Security tests: RBAC policy fuzzing, audit log tamper checks with KMS-signed entries.
User acceptance: internal SRE runbook drills using the toolbox for 5 common incident types and collect feedback.
observability_and_metrics: Session-level MTTR improvements vs baseline (target 20% reduction in first month for curated flows).
Autosuggest precision/recall measured against ground-truth chosen steps in past incidents.
Audit-log ingestion completeness and KMS-signing latency.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal dev team + 2 SRE responders (feature flag enabled) — 2 weeks.
Canary: entire SRE organization + 3 product support engineers — 3 weeks; evaluate metrics and UXR.
Beta: selected customer success accounts (opt-in) with additional telemetry retention — 4 weeks.
GA: default-off in Console, opt-in toggle for tenants; partner with Growth for messaging and docs.
